  on both**: Secret of the Silver Blades' C64 trampoline is at `$2DCB` (slot 1 of 3)
  and Gateway to the Savage Frontier's at `$2E10` (slot 24 of 32) -- exactly the raw
  words those two titles' own retail DOS `ECL*.DAX` use (Secret `$2DCB` x147 vs
  `$2E10` x1; Gateway `$2E10` x135 vs `$2DCB` x0, raw-16-bit-word scan). Null,
  denominator 65536: 1/65536 per title for the exact slot, so 2.3e-10 jointly; even
  the weakest span-only form is 2.0e-7 jointly. Controls: the metric misses when a
  title's word is scored against another title's table (4x4 cross-assignment, and

  `python tools/c64_kernel.py trampoline --title secret|gateway`.
  **This EXPLAINS the awkward fact:** `0xe804`/`$6803` is not a jump-table slot in any
  of the four titles, so it is a different addressing mechanism entirely and there is
  no reason for it to move when the table does; `$2E10`/`$2DCB` are table slots, and

  gap is two differently-built tables, **not** 23 deleted entries.

  is staged at `$0800`"), so the match identifies WHICH SLOT the operand names and
  says nothing about what that slot's staged overlay does -- the semantic label

  `FX_HAVE_FILES`/`FX_HAVE_SCRIPT` was already latched). That is worse than the ten
  placeholder opcodes above, which at least dispatch and continue. A second path is
  not gated at all: `op_if`'s false branch reaches `skip_one_instruction`, whose own
  extension list repeats the same seven values and omits `0x41`, so a guarded `0x41`
  falls through to `get_operand_meta(0x41)` and indexes `optab` at `0x41*2 = 0x82` --
  exactly one entry past a 65-row, 0x82-byte table.
  **Not established, and do not close this item by assuming either way:** which
  `.badop` arm each of the 89 sites takes was not traced. That half stands.
  **The SECOND half is SETTLED 2026-09-10 at five sites, and the superseded wording is
  quoted here rather than deleted.** It read: *"whether any retail block actually places
  `0x41` as the sole guarded instruction of a false `IF` is unknown -- the report's
  walker models a false condition as jumping straight past the guarded instruction, so
  it structurally cannot see that shape. Settling the second needs a byte-adjacency scan
  for `0x16..0x1b` immediately followed by `0x41` at a real instruction boundary."*
  That scan was run, folded into `ecl_host_call_coverage.py`'s existing CFG walk rather
  than added as a second, subtly different model of the same data, and is published as
  `guarded_0x41_after_if_census` with the prose DERIVED from it:
  **5 sites (CoK 3, DoK 2), all five with BOTH compare branches live**, out of **3,560**
  reachable `IF` sites with a decodable guarded instruction, across **47** blocks and
  **27,821** decoded instruction offsets, with **0** blocks hitting the 50,000-state cap
  and **0** truncated offsets. The five, byte-exact: CoK `ECL2.DAX` blk 50 @5529
  `18 41 00 01 02 dc 05`, blk 66 @592 `16 41 00 01 02 10 27`, blk 67 @7166
  `17 41 00 00 03 79 7f`; DoK `ECL3.DAX` blk 83 @4721 `16 41 00 01 02 88 13`, blk 99
  @2514 `18 41 00 00 02 50 c3`.
  **State it as a RANGE, never as a bare 5.** A raw byte-pair scan for `0x16..0x1b`
  followed by `0x41`, ignoring instruction boundaries entirely, finds 44 (CoK 33 /
  DoK 11) -- an upper bound, not a rival count, the same category error
  `methodology_discrepancy_demo_opcode_0x41` demonstrates for the plain opcode tally.
  So: **5 <= N <= 44** -- exactly 5 under this decoder and CFG model, at least 5 in the
  retail data.
  **Three things this does NOT establish, and the third is the one most likely to be
  dropped when the number is quoted.** (i) Whether the engine ever EXECUTES the false
  branch at these sites at runtime -- `false_branch_live` means the static walk could
  not rule the branch out, not that a playthrough takes it. (ii) The 39 raw byte-pair
  candidates this walk does not reach as instruction starts are bounded and counted, not
  decomposed one by one. (iii) The CONSEQUENCE of the out-of-bounds read: it is out of
  bounds by exactly one entry by construction, but what the two bytes past `optab`
  resolve to is INFERRED from the `-f bin` section layout, not measured. **Do NOT
  upgrade "triggerable" to "crashes".**

  that matters. The browser engine's own separately-written walker

  known model differences pull against each other (this tool prunes provably-dead IF
  edges, continues past a dynamic GOTO operand, and caps at 50,000 states per block --
  though that cap was reached by none of the 47 blocks here, so it cannot be the
  explanation). It was not decomposed per title. It does not touch the result: five
  sites under both models.
  **Do NOT cite the TypeScript run for the both-branches-live half.** `0x41` is not a
  branching opcode there, so its own fallthrough successor is the same offset as the
  IF's not-taken edge, and a flat offset-reachability set cannot separate "reached via
  the false branch" from "executed the guarded instruction and continued". That half
  rests on this tool's comparison-outcome model alone.
  All of this is a STATIC reading of `ccecl.asm` and of the retail ECL data; no DOSBox
  session was run for any of it.
  Note the frame before quoting any of this: these are DISTINCT reachable code
  offsets, not raw byte-value scans -- the naive opcode-byte scan reads CoK 302 /
  DoK 446 for the same opcode and is a different quantity.

> **▶ Format correction (2026-08-21) — read before trusting any completed DQK `MONCHA.GLB` leaf
> below.** Every member of `MONCHA.GLB` begins with a **2-byte big-endian uncompressed length**; the
> RLE stream starts at byte 2. DQK's own loader reads it (file `0x3570C`) and passes it to the
> decompressor at `00d7:0a1c` as the bounded expected output size. This project decompressed from
> byte 0, consuming that word as two RLE control bytes, so **every DQK monster record was out of
> phase by a record-dependent amount**. Header vs decoded length is now exact for **98 of 98**.
> Full account: `research/cok-m4-fidelity-plan.md` §29 (commit `df69707`); the same banner with the
> per-claim breakdown is at the top of `ROADMAP.md`. In short, for the C4.2b / E3.2a / M37 leaves:
> record lengths are **416..598, median 436** (not 88..533/321); the name is at a **fixed `0x68`**
> and the ability block at a **fixed `0x78`** in all 98 (not member-dependent, not searched for);
> there is **no record-type byte at offset 2**, so every "type-8 / non-type-8" split below describes
> an artefact (category now comes from an is-monster flag at `0x66` and race at `0x58`); full stats
> go **~20 → 86 of 98** over a **74 monster / 8 humanoid / 5 sub / 11 npc** roster;
> `reconstructDqkRecord` is off the data path (its "inline-compressed stat block" premise is false);
> the **UMBER HULK canon-AC injection is RETIRED** (AC 2 is on disk; archive-wide `acSource` = 0);
> `encodeMonchaMember` emitted no length word at all and `DQK_RECORD_LEN` went 108 → `0x1A0`; and
> the garbled names (SAUAGIN, IRON OLEM, THENOL FNATIC, SKEL WARROR, UMBERHULK, UVWW., SELIA,
> TASLEHOFF, PRINCE ALHOOK, SPECTE, WRAIT, FRE GIANT, EYE OF THE DEP, BLACK OGUE, DRK WIZARD,
> THENOL WIARD, "BAKAI SHAMAN", "SHARMAN") are **decode artefacts**, not game facts. **BAKALI
> SHAMAN is a monster with 9 hit dice, not a level-9 cleric.**

evidence remains in generated corpus reports and `docs/engine/research/`; do not replace byte-level
proof with this summary.

## Conventions
- One item ≈ one shippable slice (a few hundred LOC + tests + an e2e case). If an item is
  bigger, split it in place and do the first sub-item.
- Engine logic stays **pure** in `packages/engine`; browser/DOM in `apps/web`. New original
  screens go through the indexed-framebuffer compositors (`composeExploreScreen` family).
- Every slice: `pnpm -r exec tsc --noEmit` (0) · `vitest` green · `node apps/web/test/e2e.mjs`
  (all pass) · `pnpm build:app` + deploy + live HTTP 200 check · commit with the required
  trailers.

## Phase C — The Dark Queen of Krynn (Gen2, the target engine)
- [x] **C1** DQK **detection profile** + boot; **HLIB GEO** map decode (Gen2 container). Engine:
      reverse-engineered the Gen2 GEO format — `GEO.GLB` is a flat HLIB **DATA** library (magic=1:
      member[0] = a 20-entry id table, members[1..20] = the maps). Each map is `byte0=W, byte1=H,
      6 header bytes, then 4 planes of W×H` — variable-sized (10×10 … 39×20), unlike Gen1's fixed
      16×16, but with the **identical nibble wall semantics** (plane0=(N<<4)|E, plane1=(S<<4)|W,
      plane2=backdrop, plane3=doors; East-edge symmetry 0.85–1.00 across all 20 maps). New
      `decodeGen2GeoBlock`/`decodeGen2GeoArchive`/`sniffGen2GeoBlock` (`geo.ts`, sharing a
      `buildGeoResult` helper with the Gen1 decoder → every CoK/DoK golden byte-identical). The DQK
      detection profile already existed in `BUILTIN_PROFILES`. Web: `apps/web/src/ui/dqkExplore.ts`
      fetches GEO.GLB, `decodeHlib`→`decodeGen2GeoArchive` → 20 walkable maps, with a map picker +
      automap + keyboard movement; `?dqk=1` route, sidebar entry, and the Library boots
      `dark-queen-of-krynn/DOS` straight into it. VGA wall art is C3 (this slice is the decoded,
      walkable grid). 470 engine / 34 e2e (golden against real GEO.GLB; `?dqk=1` boot+walk case).
- [x] **C2** **Gen2 ECL** dialect deltas (disassemble DQK `DATA` blocks; opcode drift vs Gen1).
      Reversed the DQK ECL dialect: `ECL.GLB` is an HLIB **DATA** library (magic=1, id table +47
      scripts) pairing scripts to GEO maps by the shared logical area id. **The ONLY delta is the
      block header** — Gen2 drops the Gen1 `0x1388` magic word, so the header is **20 bytes** (5 far
      pointers) not 22, and `vbase = 0x8000` not `0x7FFE`; the opcode table, operand framing and
      6-bit string packing are **identical** (proof: 0/47 members carry the magic, 446 inline strings
      decode to English, area inits fire `LOAD_FILES`, area 4 prints the real *"YOUR VOYAGE BEGINS
      PEACEFULLY…"* intro). Engine: `EclDialect` + `ECL_GEN1`/`ECL_GEN2` thread through
      `disassemble.ts`/`vm.ts`/`program.ts` (default Gen1 → every CoK/DoK golden byte-identical); new
      `loaders/eclGlb.ts` (`decodeEclGlb`) → `BlockSource` by area id; GEO loader now exposes each
      map's logical area id for GEO↔ECL pairing. Web: `dqkExplore.ts` runs the entered area's script
      through the Gen2 VM and shows the fired events (`LOAD_FILES` GEO + first decoded text). Docs:
      `docs/engine/research/ecl-gen2-dqk.md`. 475 engine / 34 e2e.
- [x] **C3** DQK **VGA 256-color** graphic set through the render pipeline (HLIB TILE + palette).
      The HLIB TILE decoder + per-leaf colour table + Chain-4 layout + `indexedToRGBA` were already
      verified; the gap was **palette compositing** (the open "multi-palette layering" question). A
      DQK leaf only owns a *slice* of the DAC (measured: `ALWAYS`=0–15, `GEN`/`FRAME`=16–31,
      `BIGPIC`=32–255), so a picture rendered with only its own leaf palette leaves the other slots
      black. New engine `mergePalettes(...)`/`definedColorCount` (`render/palette.ts`) +
      `compositeHlibPalette(archive)` (`hlib.ts`) layer leaves into one 256-colour table (last-wins,
      null never clobbers, cycles concat). The full overland DAC =
      `mergePalettes(composite(ALWAYS), composite(BIGPIC))` → 240 defined slots. Web `dqkExplore.ts`
      (`?dqk=1`) now shows a **VGA art panel**: the 3 BIGPIC overland pictures (304×120, method 18)
      painted through the composited DAC with a prev/next stepper — DQK's real 256-colour art running
      through the render pipeline in the browser. Docs: `docs/engine/research/vga-palette-compositing-dqk.md`.
      480 engine / 34 e2e.
- [x] **C4.1** DQK **per-cell ECL events** fire through the engine (Gen2-dialect `SearchLocation`).
      Reverse-engineered DQK's per-cell event dispatch: unlike Gen1 (which dispatches on the cell
      backdrop byte at `0x7F79`), DQK dispatches on the **party coordinates** at low data addresses —

## Phase E6 — Close the "art not visible in-game" gate: reach a ported CoK area under DOSBox

> The art lift (E5.4/E5.5) and the content port (E3/E4) are both proven on real bytes, but every art slice carries the same honest gate: under DOSBox the rebuild boots to the **front menu** and "Begin Adventuring" loops back rather than landing in a real CoK map, because the ported area IDs don't line up with what `DQK.EXE`'s new-game entry expects. This phase attacks that reachability gap — the true critical path to *demonstrating* "best-of art on the newest engine, playable." The web engine already renders the ported maps + lifted art (e2e proves the pixels); the missing piece is the DOS executable's new-game → first-area wiring.

GEO.GLB starts at area 2; ECL entry vaddr 0x8014). **The conflict:** `buildDqkGame` maps the source DAX block id straight to the GLB area id, and **CoK's lowest ECL id is 16** (ids 16–99) — so a ported CoK `ECL.GLB` had **no area 1** and DQK.EXE's hard-coded first load would fail. **Fix (research Option A — no EXE patch):** new engine `makeEclForwardStub(target)` builds a 24-byte Gen2 ECL block (20-byte header, all far-ptrs→0x8014, body `20 00 NN` = `NEWECL #target` + `00` EXIT — **byte-faithful**: a real CoK `NEWECL #16` is exactly `20 00 10`, and CoK blocks 17/36 literally `NEWECL #16` to reach the overland, verified by decoding `ECL1.DAX` myself); `portGen1EclArchiveToGen2(entries, {entryAreaId:1})` + `planEntryStub` inject it at area 1 forwarding to the lowest real id (16) **only when absent**; `buildDqkGameData` now does this by default and reports `manifest.newGameEntry`. **Verified on REAL materialized bytes:** a built `cok-on-dqk` `DISK3/ECL.GLB` carries area ids **1,16,17,18,32,33,34,36**; area 1 = the 24-byte stub that disassembles (Gen2) to `NEWECL 16 | EXIT` at entry 0x8014 — exactly what DQK.EXE loads, so "Begin Adventuring" no longer hits a missing area. +5 engine tests (stub shape/round-trip, planEntryStub logic, real-CoK area-1 injection, empty→null). 815 engine / tsc 0 / 41 e2e; the binary menu-dispatch offset stays UNLOCATED (Borland overlay). ## Phase M7 — Real user-asset playback (AssetSource)

VISION's core promise is "plays any Gold Box game from the user's own assets," but the
Library (M0.S5/M6.S1) only ever *detected* a picked folder — `onLibrarySelect()` then
booted the game from the checked-in repo's own bundled copy (`catalog.ts#assetUrl` /
`gameData.ts`'s literal paths), never the picked folder's own bytes. `library.ts`'s own
scan even said as much: "The handle is retained so later milestones can stream the actual
asset bytes on demand" — that milestone hadn't shipped. This phase closes that gap,
game-loader by game-loader.

  - [x] **M7.S1** Wire the CoK/DoK (Gen1 DAX) explore path so a Library entry backed by a
        user-picked folder reads THAT folder's own files, not the bundled repo copy.
        _(2026-07-02.)_ New `apps/web/src/ui/assetSource.ts`: an `AssetSource` interface
        (`readAsset(basename): Promise<Uint8Array | null>`) plus a `NULL_ASSET_SOURCE`
        default. `library.ts` already opened real file handles for its magic-probe pass
        (`byBasename: Map<string, () => Promise<File>>` for the browser, `electron.
        readFile` for the desktop shell) but discarded them after detection; both are now
        also wrapped into a persistent, full-file-reading `AssetSource` attached to every
        `LibraryEntry`. `onLibrarySelect()` passes `entry.assetSource` into `startExplore
        (gameId, assetSource)`; `explore.ts`'s single asset-loading choke point
        (`fetchDaxRaw` → new `readAssetBytes()`) reads through it by basename when set,
        falling back to the existing `fetch(assetUrl(path))` bundled-copy path otherwise
        (every non-Library caller — `?explore=1`, demo, play-flow, etc. — is unaffected).
        A missing file in the picked folder is a hard error, not a silent fallback to the
        bundled copy (mixing sources would produce a misleading asset set). **Proof, not
        just plumbing:** a naive wire-up could silently no-op and still pass every existing
        test (they all boot the bundled copy). Two new tests specifically prove the
        picked-folder bytes are what gets read: (1) `apps/web/test/e2e.mjs`'s new
        "Library: booted entry reads its OWN assetSource" — a synthetic seam
        (`addFromEntriesWithAssets`) registers a Library entry with deliberately-garbage
        DAX bytes and asserts the dungeon load fails loudly (if the assetSource were
        ignored, the real bundled CoK data would load fine instead); (2) `apps/electron/
        test/e2e.mjs`'s new "booted entry reads a REAL external folder's own bytes" — a
        real copy of `Champions of Krynn/` outside the repo tree with `ECL1.DAX`
        corrupted, picked via native fs (`pickFolderForTest`), clicked through the real
        DOM Library-entry path, asserted to fail the same way — the strongest available
        proof (real external folder + real native fs + real corrupted bytes, no synthetic
        seam). tsc clean across all 5 workspace packages; all 1141 engine tests unaffected;
        all 42 pre-existing apps/web e2e cases still pass (0 regressions) + 1 new = 43/43;
        apps/electron e2e 2/2 (M6.S1's existing case + the new M7.S1 case). Deployed both
        `apps/web` and `apps/author` (shared `library.ts`). **Not done / honestly out of
        scope:** DQK's Gen2 HLIB path (`dqkExplore.ts`) has its own separate asset-fetch
        choke point and is NOT wired to `AssetSource` yet — DQK booted from the Library
        still plays the bundled copy (a clear, scoped M7.S2 candidate). The other 6
        detected-but-not-yet-playable profiles (PoR/CoAB/Gateway/Buck Rogers, M5.S6) are
        unaffected (they don't reach a playable loader at all yet, `AssetSource` or not).

  - [x] **M7.S2** Wire DQK's Gen2/HLIB explore path (`dqkExplore.ts`) to the same
        `AssetSource` mechanism M7.S1 built — the scoped follow-on M7.S1 explicitly named.
        _(2026-07-02.)_ Same pattern as M7.S1, applied to a harder surface: unlike
        `explore.ts`'s single `fetchDaxRaw` choke point, `dqkExplore.ts` had **10** separate
        `fetch(assetUrl(...))` call sites across 7 loader functions (GEO.GLB, ECL.GLB,
        MONCHA.GLB, 3× ADDQ*.XMI, INSTR.AD, SFXDQ.VOC, SOUNDS.GLB, the CoK-8X8D1.DAX chrome
        borrow, BIGPIC.TLB + ALWAYS.TLB) with varying error-tolerance (one hard-required
        throw, the rest optional-with-null-fallback). Added the same `readAssetBytes(path)`
        helper (module-level `activeAssetSource`, reused `assetSource.ts`'s `basenameOf`)
        and replaced all 10 call sites, preserving each site's original error semantics
        (`loadGeoLibrary` still throws on failure; the 6 optional loaders still degrade to
        null; `loadDqkArt`'s BIGPIC/ALWAYS concurrency preserved via `Promise.allSettled`
        instead of `Promise.all`). `startDqkExplore(assetSource?)` sets `activeAssetSource`;
        `onLibrarySelect()`'s DQK branch now passes `entry.assetSource` through. Basename
        lookup still works unchanged for DQK's DISK1/DISK2/DISK3 subfolder layout — GLB/TLB
        filenames are unique across disks, same as CoK's flat layout. **Proof:** new
        `apps/web/test/e2e.mjs` "Library: booted DQK entry reads its OWN assetSource, not
        the bundled copy (M7.S2)" — registers a Library entry via `addFromEntriesWithAssets`
        with garbage bytes for `GEO.GLB` only (the one hard-required load; `decodeHlib`
        throws immediately on a bad 4-byte HLIB signature), leaves every other DQK asset
        absent from the synthetic source (correctly exercising their null-fallback paths,
        never a silent read-through to the bundled copy), and asserts the boot fails with
        DQK's distinct "Could not load DQK dungeons: ..." status (not CoK's "Could not load
        dungeon:" — different call site, different wording, checked precisely). tsc clean
        across all 5 workspaces; 1141 engine tests unaffected; apps/web e2e 44/44 (43
        pre-existing + 1 new, 0 regressions, including the pre-existing plain `?dqk=1` boot
        case — proves the bundled-copy fallback still works when no assetSource is given);
        apps/electron e2e 2/2 unaffected (re-run to confirm no regression from the
        `dqkExplore.ts` changes). Deployed `apps/web` + `apps/author`. **M7 is now fully
        wired for both playable engine generations** (Gen1 DAX via M7.S1, Gen2 HLIB via
        M7.S2) — the remaining 6 detected profiles (PoR/CoAB/Gateway/Buck Rogers) still have
        no playable loader at all, `AssetSource` or not, so there is no further M7 slice
        until one of those gets a loader.

## Phase M8 — Amiga art-mapping studio (close Gap G5's human-in-the-loop half)

> **Why now (the one genuinely-new, in-vision slice found in the 2026-07-02 scope audit).**
> Every other tracked surface is exhausted: the only unchecked primary-goal item is
> **E6.2b-4** (DQK copy-protection, PARKED after 5 RE passes — do NOT touch it), M5/M6/M7's
> "out of scope" notes are all either broader-roster (which `VISION.md` explicitly makes
> "architected-for," not a deliverable — no real assets exist and no loader is wanted yet)
> or need real asset bytes we don't have. The exception is **Gap G5** (`docs/engine/research/
> cok-content-port-plan.md` §4). The Amiga `SPRIT*`/`PIC*`/`CPIC*`/`BODY*` art **decodes to
> real pixels today** (`daa.ts` `decodeDaa` -> `archive.subFrames[].frames[]`, each with its
> own 32-colour palette; 158/169 files render coherently), but it is stuck at
> **`shape-mismatch`** in `DQK_ART_LAYOUT` (`packages/engine/src/loaders/dqkArtMap.ts`): the
> Amiga frame set and the DQK target slot set are a *different image set* (e.g. SPRIT1.DAA =
> 17 base sprites x 3 distance frames of 88x88 monster/portrait art; DQK `SPRIT.TLB` = 96
> overworld icons of 72x25). The port plan is explicit that picking *which Amiga frame maps
> to which DQK slot* is **"a content judgment call, not a decode problem" — a HUMAN decision,
> and exactly the thing an agent must NOT guess** (guessing a mapping = a silent-wrong asset,
> the same RE-discipline violation the port plan's G5/Q3 rows forbid). So the automatable,
> in-vision work is the **tooling around that human decision**: show the decoded-but-unmapped
> Amiga frames next to the DQK target slots, let a person assign them, then mechanically
> repack the assignment. This directly serves the PRIMARY goal ("superior Amiga artwork") AND
> `VISION.md` pillar 2 (an asset resolving to multiple graphic sets) + pillar 3 (authoring).
> It bolts nothing onto the engine — `buildPortableArtOverrides`/`buildAmigaArtOverride`
> already do the portable-entry repack; this phase adds the mapping layer the `shape-mismatch`
> entries need. Numbered M8 per the loop's convention of opening a fresh milestone when the
> parked E6.2b-4 can't absorb more effort.
>
> **Deploy gotcha (memory `goldbox-build-loop`):** an `apps/web` redeploy clobbers
> `/greybox/author/` — always redeploy BOTH `apps/web` and `apps/author` and re-verify both
> live-200, even for an `apps/web`-only change.

## Phase M9 — Live graphics-mode switching IN PLAY (finish VISION pillar 2 in the exploration view)

> **Why now (the next genuinely-new, in-vision gap after the 2026-07-02 M8 close).** The
> only unchecked primary-goal item is still **E6.2b-4** (DQK copy-protection, PARKED after 5
> RE passes — do NOT touch it), and Phase M8 closed Gap G5's tooling half. Auditing what
> `VISION.md` still promises but the code does not yet deliver surfaces one clear, high-value,
> currently-open gap: **pillar 2 — "live graphics-mode switching" while actually playing** —
> which `VISION.md` calls the headline ("the user's best-of-art idea generalised into a
> feature") and which the "done enough to share" bar requires *in play* ("at least two
> switchable graphic sets, DOS EGA <-> Amiga"). Today that feature exists only as a **standalone
> title-screen A/B demo** (`apps/web/src/ui/gswitch.ts`, `?gswitch=1`), which flips EGA<->Amiga
> on the BIGPIC/CPIC/BODY *scene* art and nothing else. The actual walking-around exploration
> view (`apps/web/src/ui/explore.ts`) renders its first-person dungeon
> (`renderFirstPersonViewWithSky` -> `renderWallViewIndexed`) from a **single, fixed DOS-EGA**
> wall/sprite source and never consults a graphic set — its only `amiga` reference is the audio
> track. `ROADMAP.md` marks **M3.S2 as `◐` partial** for exactly this reason: "Full in-dungeon
> wall switch blocked on the unsolved 6-byte DAA sub-frame format (`8X8D*.DAA`)."
>
> **That blocker is now GONE.** The 6-byte sub-frame inner-pixel codec was solved end-to-end
> (`docs/engine/research/subframe-format.md`, `tools/subframe_decode.py`, 158/169 files render
> coherent full-colour art) **and ported into the live engine** — `loaders/daa.ts`'s `decodeDaa`
> now populates real pixels for the `8X8D*`/`SPRIT*` sub-frame archives (Gap G5, confirmed by
> M8.S1: `8X8D1.DAA` decodes 12 frames, `SPRIT1.DAA` 51). So the Amiga in-dungeon wall/sprite art
> a live switch needs **decodes today**. The switching *machine* also already exists and is unit-
> tested: `packages/engine/src/graphics/graphicSet.ts` (`GraphicSetManager` — pointer-swap
> `setActive`, per-frame `resolve` fallback chain, `on('change')` redraw) + `buildGraphicSet.ts`
> (positional `(category,index)` slot mapping so the DOS and Amiga sets of the *same* game line
> up). Nothing in the exploration path consumes it. This phase closes that gap: wire the existing
> `GraphicSetManager` into the real explore loop so a player flips EGA<->Amiga *while walking a
> CoK/DoK dungeon* — the headline feature, in play, not a demo. It bolts nothing new onto the
> engine's data model; it consumes machinery M1.S2 already shipped. Numbered M9 per the loop's
> convention of opening a fresh milestone when parked E6.2b-4 can't absorb more effort.
>
> **Not** in scope: DQK's own live switch (DQK ships only its DOS-VGA set — there is no second
> art platform to switch *to* for it; pillar 2 for DQK is a non-goal, like the broader roster).
> The `?gswitch=1` standalone title demo stays as-is (it is the proven A/B seam this phase reuses).
>
> **Deploy gotcha (memory `goldbox-build-loop`):** an `apps/web` redeploy clobbers
> `/greybox/author/` — always redeploy BOTH `apps/web` and `apps/author` and re-verify both
> live-200, even for an `apps/web`-only change.

> **Why now (the next genuinely-new, in-vision gap after the 2026-07-02 M9 close).** The

> RE passes — do NOT touch it), and Phases M5/M6/M7/M8/M9 delivered pillars 1, 2, 3, and 5.
> Auditing what `VISION.md` still promises but the code does not yet deliver surfaces one
> clear, high-value, currently-open gap: **pillar 4 — "Fold the GBC tool's features … into
> the engine as first-class panels"** — and the **one unmet clause** of the "done enough to
> share" bar ("plus a read-only Companion panel (auto-map + databases)" *while playing*).

> `dqkExplore.ts`) never opens any of them, and it even draws its **own** inferior bespoke
> automap that ignores Phase D1's real `Automap` model (fog-of-war + notes). This phase wires
> the already-built, already-tested D-phase compositors/models into the live play loop as
> toggleable overlays — the headline "Companion, built in," in play, not a demo. It bolts
> nothing new onto the engine's data model; it consumes machinery Phase D already shipped —

## Phase M11 — Author → distribute → play: portable module packages, playable in the Library (finish VISION pillar 3's FRUA baseline)

> **Why now (the next genuinely-new, in-vision gap after the 2026-07-03 M10 close).** The
> only unchecked items are the PARKED **E6.2b-4** (DQK copy-protection — do NOT touch) and the
> user-decision fork **M10.S4** (never auto-build). Phases A/B/C/M5–M10 delivered pillars 1, 2,
> 4, 5 and the *editing* half of pillar 3. Auditing what `VISION.md` still promises but the
> code does not yet deliver surfaces one clear, high-value, currently-open gap: **pillar 3's
> FRUA baseline — author a module, SAVE it as a portable design, SHARE it, and PLAY it** — the
> milestone VISION names immediately after the now-met play/share bar ("Authoring follows").
> Today authored modules live only in `apps/author`'s single anonymous localStorage slot: there
> is no whole-`ModulePackage` serializer, no file export/import in the author, and the player
> (`apps/web`) never imports `loadModule`/`ModulePackage` — so an authored game can be edited
> and playtested but never saved to a file, shared, or booted as a Library entry the way an
> original game is. This phase makes an authored `ModulePackage` a portable, playable artifact
> and a first-class Library entry — the exact M9/M10-shaped move (wire a built-and-tested
> mechanism into the real product loop). It bolts almost nothing new onto the engine data
> model; it consumes machinery Phase M5 + M10 already shipped. Numbered M11 per the loop's
> convention of opening a fresh milestone when parked E6.2b-4 / M10.S4 can't absorb more effort.
> Full audit: `docs/engine/research/next-phase-audit-2026-07-03-authored-module-distribution.md`.
>
> **Deploy gotcha (memory `goldbox-build-loop`):** an `apps/web` redeploy clobbers
> `/greybox/author/` — always redeploy BOTH `apps/web` and `apps/author` and re-verify both
> live-200, even for an `apps/web`-only change.
>
> **Not in scope:** any NEW authoring *capability* (M5 built the editors); the
> `packages/ui-kit`/`ui-*` extraction (ROADMAP M0.S3 — a natural follow-on once the player-side
> module host is a third real consumer, but organizational, not this phase); a hosted public
> module gallery / bundling original-derived art into shared modules (M11.S5 — a
> legal/distribution user-decision fork, flagged, NOT auto-built).

  - [x] **M11.S1** — see Done section below (2026-07-03).

  - [x] **M11.S2** — see Done section below (2026-07-03).

  - [x] **M11.S3** — see Done section below (2026-07-03).

  - [x] **M11.S4** — see Done section below (2026-07-03).

  - [ ] **M11.S5** *(optional follow-on, flag for user)* **Public module sharing / gallery, and
        whether shared modules may embed original-derived assets.** A hosted place to upload/download
        `.gbmod` files, and/or letting an exported module **embed decoded original-game art** (from a
        user's own DQK/CoK `.TLB`), crosses the project's distribution stance verbatim ("Ship the
        engine + tools only … nothing copyrighted is committed to the repo or hosted on the website").
        A public gallery that accepts user uploads potentially containing copyrighted SSI art is a
        **legal + hosting + moderation decision**, and "may an exported module embed original-derived
        art vs. author-original art only" is a policy fork. Left unstarted; surfaced here rather than
        decided.

> Pool/Curse/Hillsfar, **DoK imports CoK, DQK imports DoK** — each a field map across the layout
> drift, not a raw copy."* `apps/web/src/ui/importParty.ts`'s own file-doc header (B3, already
> shipped) calls this **"the series feature"**: *"you finish Champions of Krynn and import those
> same characters into Death Knights of Krynn (**and on into Dark Queen**)."* Only the first "on
> into" hop was ever built (`?import=cok`) — a grep for `dokToDqk`/`importDok`/any DoK-save
> consumer besides M13's read-only viewer turned up **zero code anywhere**, even though M13 had
> just wired the exact `.GAM` decoder this hop needs. `dqkParty.ts`'s `installDqkParty()` already
> guards `if (!force && getParty().length > 0) return getParty()` — i.e. it already expects an
> externally-installed party to take priority over its default Heroes-of-the-Lance roster; nothing
> had ever populated one from a DoK save. Same "machinery built, live loop doesn't consume it"
> shape M9/M10/M11 each found and closed.

> record) has no HP field at all and stores AC/damage as the unarmoured baseline, not effective

> class/level reconstructed — this hop can only carry name + the six ability scores byte-for-byte;
> class/level/HP/effective-AC are all DERIVED through the real `addnd1e-dragonlance` `createCharacter`
> path (the same one `dqkParty.ts`'s Heroes already use), not read from the save. Disclosed in the
> import summary, not silently presented as byte-faithful.

## Phase M15 — Real post-combat XP award (`calc_battle_exp`/`addExp` wiring)

> With M14.S1 shipped, the queue converged to "done except blocked/flagged" a **sixth** time. This
> re-audit first chased `M5.S4`'s own doc-comment ("Twenty of the 35 [FRUA event] types
> [shops/temples/taverns/NPCs] don't have a shop/NPC/quest data model yet — that's M5.S5") into a
> dead end: Gen1 ECL has **no native opcode** a shop/temple event could compile to and have the VM
> actually execute (no `SHOP`/`TEMPLE` case in `ecl/vm.ts` — `TREASURE`/`DAMAGE`/`ROB`/`PARLAY` all
> fall through the `default:` "surfaced and skipped" no-op path, `vm.ts:603-608`); simulating one
> honestly would mean inventing new VM behaviour no real decoded game event ever triggers, which
> conflicts with ADR-0006. Parked as a genuinely harder, murkier lift than a single slice — not
> opened as M15.
>
> The re-audit instead followed `docs/engine/research/decompile-worklist.md`'s own **ovr006**
> entry (`decompile-ovr006-xp-treasure.md`), which had already named and partially closed an
> "engine GAP": the real Champions of Krynn `calc_battle_exp`/`addExp` formula (rolled-HP XP + flat
> XP + gold's XP worth + magic-item-plus XP, split with a single-class +10% prime-requisite bonus /
> multiclass ÷N rule) was **implemented and tested** on 2026-06-27
> (`ruleset/addnd1e/experience.ts`, 17 passing cases) but its own doc said *"Remaining wire-up: have
> the combat-end path feed real defeated-enemy/loot data ... and apply the awards to each
> character's `exp`"* — and grep confirmed **zero call sites** for `calcBattleExp`/
> `awardCombatExperience`/`characterXpShare` outside their own test file. All three live combat
> engines (`combat/combat.ts`, `combatStepper.ts`, `combat/tactical.ts`) still summed
> `xpAwarded += target.xp ?? 0` — a flat per-kill total with no gold/item-plus XP — and
> `apps/web/src/ui/party.ts`'s `awardPartyXp` split that total dead-even across the living, with no
> prime-requisite bonus and no multiclass division. Same "machinery built, live loop doesn't
> consume it" shape M9/M10/M11/M14 each found and closed — this time on the PRIMARY-goal-adjacent
> combat/XP path itself, not an authoring nicety.
>
> **Honest scope note.** `calcBattleExp`'s `perHpXp`/`rolledHp` terms need a monster-record field
> (COAB `field_13E`) that `loaders/monster.ts` has never byte-located — only the flat `xp` field
> (offset 304) is decoded. `calcBattleExp` degrades correctly when those are omitted (adds `flatXp`
> alone), so this slice wires the formula with what's actually decoded today; per-enemy XP itself is
> therefore unchanged from before, and the real, new behaviour this slice adds is: gold's XP worth,
> magic-item-plus XP (currently 0 — the loot table has no magic drops yet, so this term is honestly
> inert until one exists), the prime-requisite +10% bonus, and the multiclass ÷N split. Locating
> `field_13E` for full HD-scaled per-enemy XP is a separate, harder byte-location task, left open.

  - [x] **M15.S1** — see Done section below (2026-07-03).

> `ovr022` shop-economy formulas — buy-price tier scaling, sell bulk penalty, coin denominations,

> same shape:

>   `value` byte AND a per-shop `tierMask` — neither exists as verified data (the current
>   `ITEM_PRICE` numbers are themselves admitted CANDIDATE guesses). Reusing those same numbers as

>   from one flat number to a multi-slot pool everywhere it's read/displayed — also bigger than a
>   wiring slice. **Not built this round.**
> - **Stacked-item sell bulk penalty** (`sellOffer`) — the one piece that IS pure wiring: the
>   existing `sellFromLeader` action already decrements a stack one unit at a time using the same
>   CANDIDATE `ITEM_PRICE` numbers already in place (no new data invented), and classic Gold Box
>   UX sells a selected stack in ONE action, not N clicks. Correcting `sellFromLeader` to sell the
>   WHOLE entry at once through the verified bulk formula is a genuine mechanics correction with

## Phase M35 — ECL `ADD_NPC` (0x36): recruit a named companion into the party (`EclVm` opcode → `dungeon.npcJoins` → `explore.ts` party-fold)

> Queue converged a **26th** time. `opcodes.ts` has carried `0x36: { wordSet: 2, mnemonic: 'ADD_NPC' }`
> since M2.S1, but the VM never had a case for it — it fell into the generic `unhandled` bucket. COAB's
> `CMD_AddNPC` (`ovr003.cs:1769`) loads a monster record by id then OVERWRITES its `control_morale` with
> `(operand>>1) + NPC_Base`, which round-trips through this engine's own `decodeMorale` back to exactly
> the ECL operand — i.e. the operand IS the effective morale%, replacing the record's own stored value.
> Fix: VM emits a new `addNpc` effect; `loadDungeon()` collects them into a new `npcJoins` field;
> `explore.ts` resolves each via the already-built `monsterLookup`, folds them into combat via the
> already-tested `monsterCombatant(rec, `n${blockId}`, 'party')` (the `n`-prefix keeps them off
> `party.ts`'s persistent roster — protected by its `idx >= roster.length` bounds check, not an
> integer-parse failure as first assumed). **Independently re-verified at implementation time** (per
> this project's standing discipline) and found the audit's core reachability claim wrong: DoK's real
> site (ECL1 block 2) does NOT boot cleanly today — `loadDungeon()` throws, because block 2's own
> `LOAD_PIECES` names WALLDEF block id 2, which `WALLDEF1.DAX` doesn't ship (only block 1). The planned
> `?eclBlock=` diagnostic was implemented, then reverted once this was found (no working target left to
> demonstrate). Proof instead: golden `EclVm.run()` tests against both real sites' raw bytes (WALLDEF-
> independent), a synthetic `loadDungeon()`/`npcJoins` test, a real-record `monsterCombatant` join test,
> and a new `injectAlly()` diagnostic seam (resolves real DoK id 48/SIR DRYDEN via `monsterLookup`,
> bypassing the broken ECL/WALLDEF chain) proving the web-side fold end-to-end. Full audit + correction
> addendum in `docs/engine/research/m35-audit.md`.

> Queue converged a **56th** time — the research subagent tried sibling-function doc-comment mining
> extremely broadly (`party.ts`'s `*ForMember` family confirmed exhausted across M63-M65; two dozen
> other files checked with no fresh candidate) and a fresh batch of pre-M40 verdict re-checks (also
> nothing new), then fell back to re-reading M54's own rejected-alternatives table line-by-line: M54
> had bundled four `MonsterRecord` fields together as "needs new UI surfaces per field" —
> `conSaveBonus`/`itemPluses`/`carriedItems`/`preparedSpellIds`. Three of the four were individually
> shipped or re-examined since (M55's Spells row, M56's Bonus XP row, `carriedItems` correctly left as
> a weaker follow-up), but `conSaveBonus` itself was never revisited — a follow-through gap, not a
> principled rejection. **Lead's own review caught an important wrinkle the research round missed**:
> `conSaveBonus` had *already* been individually investigated and declined once before, by M43
> (re-confirmed M61) — not for lacking a real consumer, but specifically because a bare "+N" row next
> to the existing `Save` row risks a player misreading it as modifying the printed save *target*

> added to the monster's own d20 *roll* before comparing to that target. M43's own text proposed the

> +2 (roll)' instead of a bare number") — so the lead implemented the same underlying fix the research
> found, but labelled the new row **"Save Roll"** (not the research doc's literal "Con Save"), which
> reads unambiguously as a roll-time bonus rather than a target change, directly resolving the
> standing objection instead of re-shipping the exact ambiguity M43/M61 had blocked. The research
> round's test-file citation was also corrected during implementation: `monsterCategory()` lives in
> apps/web (not the engine package), so its existing row-addition precedent (M38/M43's own

> branches reach real buttons in `moduleExplore.ts`) then re-read every real call site of the loop's own
> most heavily-mined territory, `RangeBracket`/`rangeTag()` (M25/M44/M48-M52), end to end rather than
> assuming "examined 6 times" meant "every branch checked". Found the one un-mined corner: `combat.ts`'s
> `logEvents()` fully differentiates a **hit** `attack` event by `coupDeGrace`/`opportunity`/`backstab`/
> `rear`/`rangeBracket` (`combat.ts:607-614`), but its sibling `else` (miss) branch (`615-618`) collapsed
> all of them into one undifferentiated `"X misses Y."` — even though `tactical.ts`'s `resolveHit()` miss
> push (`1144-1145`) already carries `rear`/`rangeBracket` exactly as the two hit pushes do (`1146-1155`,
> `1157-1167`), and `triggerGuardReactions()` (`1393-1394`) tags **every** event `opportunity: true`
> unconditionally — hit or miss, no `if (e.hit)` guard. The `opportunity` case is the most user-visible:
> a guard's readied reaction spends the action whether or not it connects, so a whiffed reaction read
> exactly like an ordinary swing even though the player had already seen the "Guarding" cyan marker
> (M71) vanish. `rangeBracket` on a miss is genuinely informative too — the range modifier was already
> folded into `needed` before the very roll that produced the miss (`1131`), so a player missing
> repeatedly at long range got no textual explanation why, the same "silent uninformative failure" class
> M72 flagged for movement's `'edge'` case. Fixed additively, reusing `rangeTag()` verbatim (already
> returns `''` for medium range, preserving the existing generic line for an ordinary miss) with the same
> `opportunity > rear > missile` priority order the hit branch uses. One real, adjacent, but explicitly
> NOT-fixed gap flagged for a future round: `backstab` isn't merely unread on a miss, `tactical.ts:1145`'s
> miss push never writes the key at all — an engine-side omission, a different class of finding than a
> display gap, out of a research-only round's remit. Full audit in `docs/engine/research/m73-audit.md`;
> all citations independently re-verified against current source (not just the audit's own excerpts)
> before implementing, per this loop's standing discipline.

## Phase M74 — `apply()`'s own action-dispatch plumbing silently drops round-boundary tick events (`regen`, `status`-expiry) from its return value, even though `logEvents()` already has correct, untriggered code for both

> Queue converged a **65th** time. First re-read the `cast`/`hazard`/`turn`/`status`(morale) branches to
> hunt a fresh M73-style sibling-`if/else` gap in `logEvents()` — found them all already exhaustive of
> their real construction sites. Widened to the FULL `TacticalEventType` union (14 members,
> `tactical.ts:343-344`) against `logEvents()`'s `switch` and found something one layer BELOW the UI: two
> members, `'regen'` and `'status'`'s `expired` half, are real, engine-computed, mechanically-live events
> that structurally never reach `apply()`'s return value at all — not a missing UI field-read (M69-M73's
> shape), but the events themselves never surviving the trip through the engine's own public action API.
> `beginRound()` (`tactical.ts:964-976`) ticks regen (`tickRegen()`, `813-819`) and status-expiry
> (`tickStatuses()`, `822-839`), pushing both to the shared `log` array — but `beginRound()` is only ever
> invoked from `positionCursor()` (`1019-1038`), and every one of `positionCursor()`'s callers discards its
> side effects as a bare `void` statement; `apply()`'s own explicit `case 'endTurn': endTurn();
> return [];` (was `1816-1818`) proved this concretely — it unconditionally returned `[]` regardless of
> what round transition (and regen/status ticking) had just fired inside that very call. `logEvents()`'s
> `case 'status':`'s `e.expired && e.inflicted` branch (`634-637`) was fully correct, tested-looking code
> that had been DEAD since the mechanic shipped — reachable only if a `type:'status', expired:true` event
> ever arrived, which it never did. `'regen'` had no case at all. Fixed at the true root: `apply()` now
> records `log.length` before dispatch and returns `log.slice(startLen)` at every exit instead of a
> hand-assembled array — sound because every resolver already `log.push()`es exactly what it returns
> (verified for all ~10 resolvers before adopting this), so the fix is a strict superset for every
> already-working path, confirmed by the full 1351-test suite passing unchanged after the refactor. Added
> the missing `case 'regen':` to `logEvents()`; the `status` case needed no change, it just started firing
> for real. **Independently discovered during implementation, beyond the audit's own explicit finding**:
> the same root cause ALSO silently dropped `beginTurn()`'s own per-turn hazard/morale-break checks
> (`applyHazardTo`/`applyMoraleOutcome` calls at `beginTurn()`, `987`/`990`) — both already logged, both
> now correctly surfaced by the same general fix, not a separate patch. Also corrected a prior round's
> partly-wrong "Confirmed wired" verdict: `m55-audit.md` asserted status narration was fully wired,
> re-quoted forward uncritically by `m68-audit.md` — true for infliction, silently false for expiry, per
> this round's own re-trace (not just a grep-for-existence check). Full audit in
> `docs/engine/research/m74-audit.md`; every citation independently re-verified against current source,
> including reading every resolver's own `log.push`/return pairing before adopting the `log.slice` shape,
> per this loop's standing discipline.

## Phase M76 — a missed backstab attempt narrates identically to an ordinary rear-arc miss, because `resolveHit()`'s miss push never records `backstab` even though the boolean is computed two lines above it

> Queue converged a **67th** time. Tried M75's own newest technique (a fresh typed accept/reject gate
> function with N call sites, only some routing through it) against `character.ts`'s
> `createCharacter()`/`ValidationResult` and `shop.ts`'s `buyItem()`/`sellItem()`/`ShopTxn` — both
> traced end to end and found already fully wired, no gap. Fell to this round's own priority 2: the
> `backstab`-on-miss engine gap that M73 first found and precisely characterized, that M74 re-verified
> and consciously deferred (a scope choice, not a rejection), and that M75 carried forward unchanged.
> Re-read `tactical.ts`/`combat.ts` at current line numbers and confirmed the gap is still exactly as
> M73 described, byte-for-byte unchanged since the original CT.5c commit and untouched even by M73's
> own commit that fixed the miss branch's `rear`/`rangeBracket`/`opportunity` handling. `resolveHit()`'s
> miss-branch event push (`tactical.ts:1145`) never wrote a `backstab` key at all — unlike its two
> sibling hit-branch pushes, which both write `backstab: backstab || undefined` — even though the
> boolean is computed and used to adjust the to-hit roll two lines earlier in the same function
> (`tactical.ts:1121`, `if (backstab) needed -= 4;`). `combat.ts`'s `logEvents()` differentiates a HIT
> by `coupDeGrace`/`opportunity`/`backstab`/`rear`/`rangeBracket` but its sibling miss branch had no
> `backstab` case — so a thief lining up a genuine backstab and rolling low got the identical
> "misses (from behind)" text as any non-thief rear-arc miss, even though the attack took the thief's
> own +4/×N backstab math, not the generic rear bonus. Fixed both halves: added
> `backstab: backstab || undefined` to the miss push, and a new `else if (e.backstab)` branch to
> `logEvents()`'s miss case, positioned ahead of the existing `rear` check (mirroring the hit branch's
> own backstab-before-rear priority), since a genuine backstab always also sets `fromRear`. This closes
> a gap that persisted across three rounds (M73→M74→M75→M76) purely because each intervening round had
> a stronger or differently-scoped candidate to spend its slot on — not a process failure, the standing-
> candidate backlog discipline working as intended. Full audit in `docs/engine/research/m76-audit.md`;
> every citation independently re-verified against current source, including a new permanent engine
> test proving the miss-branch event now carries `backstab: true` alongside the pre-existing `rear: true`.

## Phase M77 — `applyFlee()` never triggers a readied Guard's reaction strike after relocating a fleeing combatant, even though its sibling relocation resolver `applyMove()` always does

> Queue converged a **68th** time. Pursued priority 1 first: re-read `applyFlee()` in full to answer
> M74's own explicitly left-open question ("does it have its own version of the `apply()` log-drop
> bug, or is M74's `log.slice(startLen)` fix already sufficient?"). Verdict: no bug there —
> `applyFlee()`'s local `events` accumulator is always an exact subset of what it `log.push()`es, and
> `applyFlee` has exactly one call site in the whole engine (`apply()`'s own `case 'flee'`), so M74's
> fix already fully covers it. That closed the specific question cleanly, but reading `applyFlee()`
> and its sibling `applyMove()` side by side to answer it surfaced a different, fresh gap:
> `applyMove()` (`tactical.ts:1359-1374`) always chains BOTH post-move consequence checks after
> relocating a combatant — `applyHazardTo()` and `triggerGuardReactions()` — while `applyFlee()`
> (`tactical.ts:1403-1432`), which relocates onto the identical grid via the identical
> `reachableCells()` machinery, called only the first of the two. `git show 97597737` (the original
> CT.7d commit that introduced `triggerGuardReactions()`, a real, tested, byte-grounded "readied
> Guard gets a free reaction strike" mechanic) proved this was never a deliberate omission — the
> commit's diff only touches `applyMove()`; `applyFlee` doesn't appear in it at all, and no commit
> since ever added the call. Reachable in ordinary play: the single-figure `flee` action is exactly
> what the built-in AI uses for every morale-broken monster's rout (`aiAction()`'s `forcedFlee`
> branch), so any monster that breaks and routs past a party member's readied Guard got a completely
> free pass it would NOT have gotten had it simply moved there instead. Fixed with one additive line
> inside `applyFlee()`'s existing `else` branch, in the exact same conditional scope as the
> already-shipped hazard check it sits beside: `events.push(...triggerGuardReactions(actor));`. No UI
> changes needed — `combat.ts`'s `opportunity` attack-log branch already narrates whatever
> `applyFlee` now produces. Full audit in `docs/engine/research/m77-audit.md`; every citation
> independently re-verified against current source, including reading `applyMove`/`applyFlee`/
> `triggerGuardReactions` in full and confirming via `git show`/`git log -p -L` that the omission has
> been present, unexamined, since the mechanic's very first commit.

## Phase M78 — a destroyed undead's `xp` never reached `xpAwarded`, unlike every other kill path in `tactical.ts`

> Queue converged a **69th** time. Applied M77's own newest technique fresh: hunted for another pair
> of structurally-parallel resolvers where one calls a shared post-action consequence check and its
> sibling doesn't — this time widened past relocation resolvers to every function in `tactical.ts`
> that can **kill** a combatant. `applyHpLoss()` (`tactical.ts:1186-1194`) is the one shared "someone
> died" helper — melee, missile, spell, and hazard damage all route through it, so `xpAwarded` is
> incremented automatically. Exactly one path bypasses it on purpose: the coup-de-grace instant-kill
> (`tactical.ts:1146-1156`), which manually re-adds the identical `xpAwarded += target.xp ?? 0` line
> since it must skip `applyHpLoss()`'s gen1 overkill gate entirely. `applyTurn()`'s Turn Undead
> `'destroy'` outcome (`tactical.ts:1563-1567`) is a THIRD kill-bypass branch, structurally identical
> in shape and reason (an unconditional instant-kill that must not be gated by the `dmg ≥ hp+10`
> check) — but it never got the XP line. `git show b14238e` (the original CT.5b commit) proves the
> branch has read this way, untouched, since 2026-06-23; `git show 9845cd0` (CT.7j, ~6.5 hours later
> the same day) proves a sibling commit correctly re-derived the exact same XP line for its own new
> bypass branch — proof this was an oversight, not a design choice. Destroying a weak undead outright
> is the routine, better outcome of a successful Turn Undead check for a mid-level cleric against
> CoK/DoK's low-HD undead (Skeletons, Zombies, Wights, Ghouls), so this silently under-counted
> `xpAwarded` in ordinary play. Morale is unaffected — `apply()`'s `'turn'` case already re-sweeps
> morale unconditionally right after `applyTurn()` returns (`tactical.ts:1806-1809`); only the XP
> bookkeeping was missing. `xpAwarded` is a real consumer chain: `TacticalResult.xpAwarded` →
> `combat.ts`'s `asCombatResult()` → the `onEnd` callback → a player-visible `⚔ Victory +N XP` status
> line in `explore.ts`/`dqkExplore.ts`/`wilderness.ts`. Honest scope: the party's real roster-XP total
> is computed independently in `finalize()` from every enemy present regardless of fate, so this bug
> only undercounts the narrower `xpAwarded` tally — but that tally IS what the dismiss-time status
> line displays. Fixed with one additive line mirroring the coup-de-grace precedent exactly:
> `if (u.side === 'enemy') xpAwarded += u.xp ?? 0;`. Explicitly rejected refactoring the branch to
> call `applyHpLoss()` instead — since `dmg` would equal `hpBefore` exactly, `applyHpLoss()`'s own
> `dmg >= hpBefore + 10` gate could never fire, silently reclassifying every destroyed undead as
> `'unconscious'` (revivable) instead of `'dead'` (permanent), breaking an explicit invariant the
> existing comment states. Full audit in `docs/engine/research/m78-audit.md`; every citation
> independently re-verified against current source, including reading `applyHpLoss`/the coup-de-grace
> branch/`applyTurn`/`apply()`'s `'turn'` case in full and confirming via grep that these are the
> only two `xpAwarded +=` sites in the entire file.

## Phase M79 — an `asleep` figure that survived a damage SPELL stayed incorrectly flagged asleep, unlike the identical case via melee/missile — feeding the engine's own coup-de-grace instant-kill gate

> Queue converged a **70th** time. `tactical.ts`'s own top-level doc comment (lines 99-111) states an
> unqualified general invariant for its status flags: the engine "ticks them down each round ... and
> clears them when they expire (and wakes `asleep` figures that take damage)" — no distinction by
> damage source. Checking that claim against the actual code (comments lie, code doesn't) found it
> true for exactly one of the engine's three damage-application call sites. `resolveHit()`
> (melee/missile, `tactical.ts:1157-1168`) always calls `clearStatus(target, 'asleep')` right before
> `applyHpLoss()` — proven by the existing, already-passing test `'an asleep (helpless) target is
> auto-hit by a MISSILE and wakes when it survives the shot'` (`tactical.test.ts:443-457`).
> `applyCast()`'s spell-damage branch (`tactical.ts:1329-1338`) calls the exact same `applyHpLoss()`
> but never clears `asleep` at all — confirmed via `grep -n "clearStatus"`, which returns only
> `resolveHit()`'s two call sites in the entire file. `git log -L` on both blocks confirmed
> `applyCast()`'s damage branch has never contained the call since status effects were introduced
> (CT.5a) — this isn't a later regression, it simply never had it. Reachable in real, ordinary,
> shipped play: Sleep is a real, memorizable, combat-castable spell (`combatSpells.ts:74`), reached
> through the real party-import bridge (`party.ts`'s `combatSpellsForMember()`), and a damage spell
> (Magic Missile/Fireball) that doesn't kill the target is equally real — the player-facing auto-
> targeter (`combat.ts`'s `partyCast()`, `combat.ts:911`) doesn't exclude an asleep foe, so a
> Sleep-then-damage-spell sequence against the same stationary target is an ordinary two-turn play
> pattern, not a contrived setup. The consequence is mechanically real, not cosmetic: a figure left
> incorrectly `asleep` is still `helpless` by the engine's own gate (`tactical.ts:1136`), which (a)
> skips its own next turn (`tactical.ts:1035`) and (b) turns the very next ordinary melee swing
> against it into an unconditional CT.7j coup-de-grace instant kill (`tactical.ts:1143-1156`) — a real
> instant-kill firing purely because a spell "forgot" to wake its target, not because it was actually
> still asleep by the engine's own stated design. Fixed with one additive line mirroring
> `resolveHit()`'s exact precedent and ordering: `if (t.flags.has('asleep')) clearStatus(t,
> 'asleep');` before `applyHpLoss(t, dmg)`. Explicitly did NOT extend this to `held` — magical hold
> deliberately persists through damage (`resolveHit()`'s own comment, already correctly tested).
> A sibling gap in `applyHazardTo()` was found but left unfixed since no production path can
> currently trigger a damaging hazard at all (the same reachability standard M78 applied to its own
> analogous hazard/morale-sweep candidate). Full audit in `docs/engine/research/m79-audit.md`; every
> citation independently re-verified against current source, including reading `resolveHit()`,
> `applyCast()`, and the existing missile-wake test in full, and confirming via grep that
> `clearStatus` has exactly two call sites (both inside `resolveHit()`) before this round's fix.

## Phase M80 — a feared PARTY member's turn was silently handed the ordinary menu instead of the engine's own forced-flee AI, unlike a feared ENEMY

> Queue converged a **71st** time. `tactical.ts`'s own top-level doc comment (lines 99-111) states
> another unqualified general invariant: "feared" figures can't attack and flee toward the nearest
> edge on their turn — no distinction by side. The engine-side half of this is fully correct and
> already side-agnostic: `beginTurn()` (`tactical.ts:991`) sets `forcedFlee = actor.flags.has('feared')`
> with no side check, and `aiAction()` (`tactical.ts:1598`) checks `forcedFlee` as its very first
> branch, before any enemy-specific targeting heuristics run — proven by the existing, already-passing
> engine test `'a feared figure cannot attack and the AI makes it flee'` (`tactical.test.ts:505-513`).
> But the UI's own turn dispatcher, `advanceTurn()` (`apps/web/src/ui/combat.ts:690-717`), decided
> whether to auto-resolve a turn through that AI using only `actor.side === 'enemy'` — never also
> checking `actor.flags.has('feared')`. So a feared ENEMY was correctly auto-flee'd, but a feared PARTY
> member fell through to the ordinary `party-menu` phase, silently offering Guard/Wait/Move as if
> nothing were wrong — none of `partyGuardWait()`, `partyFlee()`, or `enterMoveMode()` has any `feared`
> guard of its own, independently confirmed by reading all three. Reachability was traced end-to-end
> before finalizing: a real DoK monster (id 20, `MON1WIZ.DAX`) carries Fear (raw spell id 84) in its
> real memorized spellbook, crosswalked (`dokSpellCrosswalk.ts:38`) to a real castable `TacticalSpell`
> (`combatSpells.ts:62,78`), wired into the real dungeon-encounter pipeline (`gameData.ts:109`,
> `explore.ts:1567/1604`, `combat.ts:325-358`'s `makeTC`) — the AI's offensive-cast heuristic will cast
> it, and a failed save (`inflictStatus`) inflicts `feared` on a real party member. This is a variant of
> the M79 scope but on a CONTROL-PATH axis rather than a per-function axis: the same doc comment's
> `feared` clause was honored by the engine's own AI but not by the UI layer that decides whether to
> invoke it — "visible on the panel" (M69) and "enforced" (M80) are independent questions, as are
> "narration plumbing" (M74) and "underlying state" (M79), reinforced a third time. Fixed by widening
> `advanceTurn()`'s dispatch condition to `actor.side === 'enemy' || actor.flags.has('feared')`, reusing
> the exact same, already-tested `aiAction()` call verbatim — a zero-engine-risk, pure UI-dispatch
> change; no `packages/engine/` file was touched this round, a first for this session. Checked the doc
> comment's remaining clauses too (`hasted`/`slowed`'s single shared `effectiveInitiative()` call site,
> `fled`'s single shared `isActive()` predicate across 13 call sites) and found both clean — per this
> round's own audit, `tactical.ts:99-111` is now considered fully exhausted (asleep: M79, feared: M80,
> hasted/slowed/fled: clean). Since this is the first PURE UI-dispatch fix this session (the engine
> test suite alone cannot regression-guard a dispatch-condition bug that lives entirely in
> `apps/web/src/ui/combat.ts`), added a new test-only seam pair (`forceFeared(id)`, mirroring the
> existing `setMenu` test-mutator precedent, plus `redispatch()` to re-invoke `advanceTurn()`) and a new
> dedicated e2e test proving the real dispatcher — not just the isolated `aiAction()` unit — now moves
> control off a feared party member instead of waiting on a menu for it. Full audit in
> `docs/engine/research/m80-audit.md`; every citation independently re-verified against current source,
> including reading `advanceTurn()`, `beginTurn()`, `aiAction()`, `legalActions()`, the existing
> enemy-side `feared` test, and confirming via grep that `forcedFlee` has exactly the four expected
> occurrences and that none of `partyGuardWait`/`partyFlee`/`enterMoveMode` has a hidden `feared` check.

## Phase M81 — a real monster's decoded Intelligence score never reached the morale-break smart-surrenders/dumb-routs mechanic built to consume it

> self-aware deferral is a HIGHER-value candidate than a fresh find"), this round reopened the
> oldest continuously-carried standing candidate in the whole loop's backlog: `TacticalCombatant.int`,
> flagged by M71 and silently carried, unpicked, through ten straight rounds (M71-M80). `monster.ts`'s
> `readAbilities()` (`loaders/monster.ts:342-345`) decodes a real, byte-verified, genuinely-variable
> Int score for every Krynn monster (verified this round against real `MON1CHA.DAX` bytes: CoK's
> GIANT SNAKE = 3, STRANGBOURN = 14; DoK's SKEL WARRIOR = 3, BLACK MAGE = 17) — into
> `MonsterRecord.abilities.int`, a required field. `tactical.ts`'s `moraleBreakOf()` (`:899-911`) has
> an already-implemented, already-unit-tested (`combatFormation.test.ts`'s pre-existing "morale Int>5
> surrender vs rout" describe block) branch that reads `TacticalCombatant.int` to classify a broken
> monster's outcome per ovr010 `FleeCheck_001` (smart `int>5` surrenders, dumb routs) instead of the
> legacy fight-circumstance fallback. But `monsterCombatant()` (`combat/combat.ts:304-345`) — the
> shared function every real encounter's `spawnEnemies()` (`combat/encounter.ts:48-60`) calls to turn
> a decoded `MonsterRecord` into a battle-ready `Combatant` — had no `abilities`/`int` field in its
> parameter type at all, so the value was silently dropped between "decoded from the game's own
> bytes" and "handed to the tactical engine," for every enemy in every real fight in the entire game.
> `git log -S "FleeCheck_001"` traced this to commit `1551717` (2026-06-30), which added the rule +
> its isolated unit test but never touched `combat/combat.ts` or `apps/web/src/ui/combat.ts` — an
> incomplete wiring (rule shipped, data plumbing not), not a deliberate faithfulness choice, per the
> code comment's own "so existing callers are unchanged" framing (an intended-future-wiring signal,
> not a permanent-omission one). This is an observable behavioral bug, not cosmetic: the real rule

> this required **zero call-site changes** — `encounter.ts` and every other caller starts supplying
> real Int data automatically, exactly like M78's/M79's xpAwarded/clearStatus fixes were single
> additive lines, but this one needed no call-site edit at all since the source data was already
> structurally present at every real call site. `apps/web/src/ui/combat.ts`'s `makeTC()` needed no
> change either — it already spreads `...c`, so `.int` now carries through automatically, the same
> free-ride pattern `regenPerRound`/`halfDamage`/`conSaveBonus`/`monsterSpellSave` already established.

## Phase M82 — DQK's own real, shipped `PARTYSTRENGTH → IF_GE → COMBAT` encounter gates (areas 18/23) were permanently unopenable — the ECL VM option that feeds them was never supplied by the one real production caller

> Queue converged a **73rd** time. `docs/engine/research/combat-trigger-c4.2b-2b-2b.md`'s disassembly
> of the real `The Dark Queen of Krynn/DISK3/ECL.GLB` confirms area 18 ("Hizden hamlet") and area 23
> ("Dargaard Keep") both run a real `PARTYSTRENGTH c12:128 ; IF_GE ; COMBAT` sequence — a wandering
> encounter gated on party power. `packages/engine/src/ecl/vm.ts`'s `case 0x1d` implements this
> faithfully and is already unit-tested both directions (`vm.test.ts:269-296`): it compares a
> host-supplied `EclVmOptions.partyStrength` against the operand threshold, defaulting to `0` when
> unsupplied (a documented, deliberately-conservative "gate never spuriously opens" default, not a
> permanent design choice — the option's own doc comment: "the host supplies whatever scalar it
> uses to gauge party power"). But `apps/web/src/ui/dqkExplore.ts`'s `fireSearchLocation()` — the
> real per-step function every player move dispatches through (`applyMove` → `runStepEvent` →
> `fireSearchLocation`) — never set this option at either of its two VM-construction call sites,
> confirmed via `grep -rn "partyStrength" apps/web/src` returning zero hits anywhere in the shipped
> app. So every real player who ever reaches area 18's or 23's trigger cell sees nothing happen where
> the game's own shipped bytes say an encounter check should run — silently, permanently, with no
> error and (until this round) no test that could catch it. This is the same "isolated-tested
> mechanism, starved of real production data" shape M81 found in `monsterCombatant()`, this time in
> the ECL VM rather than the tactical combat layer — and notably in a case where the TYPE already
> supported the field end-to-end (`SearchLocationOptions extends Omit<EclVmOptions,'entry'>`,
> `dungeonEvents.ts:101`, with `primeHandler`'s `{...opts, memory, entry}` spread already carrying it
> through) but no real caller had ever populated it. Confirmed via `git`/doc cross-reference that the

> excludes `partyStrength` via `Pick<...>`, but M36/M37's own prior audits already proved DoK's real
> `ECL1.DAX` corpus never lets an `IF_*` read this comparison at all (CoK emits the opcode zero times;
> all 4 real DoK sites get overwritten or exit first) — so only the DQK side has a live consumer to
> fix. Fixed by computing a party-power proxy from data the engine already has — the real (or demo)
> party's total max HP via the existing `dqkParty()` helper — and threading it into both of
> `fireSearchLocation()`'s VM constructions. The true original formula/units are confirmed
> unrecoverable from disk (an undocumented opcode, opaque operand encoding, no hackdocs entry); the
> fix does not claim historical accuracy, only that *some* party-derived, monotonically-power-
> correlated value is strictly more faithful than a permanent `0` that can never satisfy `IF_GE`.
> Explicitly rejected: wiring the other five ability-adjacent candidates or picking a "more correct"
> formula (none recoverable, any reasonable proxy satisfies the documented contract); widening the
> inert Gen1 `RunChainOptions` (flagged as a future consistency cleanup, not urgent, since M36/M37
> already proved it's currently a no-op for every real CoK/DoK script); and implementing the sibling
> `SURPRISE` (0x23) opcode, which has no case at all yet (a larger, different-shaped gap — an
> unimplemented mechanism, not an unfed one). Since `apps/web` has no unit-test harness of its own,
> added a new e2e-only seam accessor (`window.__dqk.partyStrength()`) and a new e2e assertion proving
> the value is now a real, positive, party-derived number rather than the permanent `0` — the existing
> `vmRun1At` liveness probe couldn't catch this (it deliberately doesn't land on the exact real
> trigger cell; it only proves the handler runs without throwing). Full audit in

> the wrong invariant — `// dead — never heals` on a bare `{hp:0}` object — one week after CT.7h had

> in-game days of rest never moved an unconscious member's HP by a single point; the only working
> recoveries left were the Temple's level-scaled Raise Dead fee or a `revive`-kind spell. Fixed with three
> small, additive edits along the natural layering (engine primitive → web accumulator → web sizing
> filter): `RestHealable` gained an optional `dead` flag, `restPartyTicks()` now threads real permadeath
> status (`deadStore`) through instead of raw `hp ≤ 0`, and `explore.ts`'s rest-sizing filter dropped its
> redundant `hp > 0` exclusion. No test needed flipping for behavior it didn't previously pin; updated the
> one test whose comment asserted the wrong invariant and added a new positive case + a new e2e assertion
> proving an unconscious member actually recovers. Two closely-related sibling gaps (the Temple's cheap-
> heal filter; Cure-spell targeting) share the identical root conflation but were deliberately left for a
> future round to keep this slice minimal. Full audit in `docs/engine/research/m89-audit.md`.

> member, and Raise Dead correctly refuses her until a real permadeath is seeded. Full audit in

> permissive level table (mostly uncapped for humans/elves) — a blind wire-in would fix CoK/DoK but
> regress DQK. Fixed additively: `checkTraining()` (engine, ruleset-agnostic) gained an optional
> `levelCap` number; `trainMember()`/`trainingStatus()` compute it via `maxLevel()` only when a new
> `enforceLevelCap` flag (default **true**) is set; `startTown()` threads that flag from its 4 call
> sites — `dqkExplore.ts`'s single DQK call site passes **false**, explicitly preserving DQK's current
> (correct, per its own manual) unbounded training, while CoK/DoK's 3 call sites keep the default,
> newly-correct enforcement. New engine unit tests + 2 new e2e cases (one proving the real CoK refusal,

## Phase M95 — the DoK→DQK import's level-inference clamp is a stale workaround, already misderives 3 of 6 real bundled saves

> Queue converged an 86th time — a direct continuation of a question M93 itself named in its own
> "Open questions" (*"worth tightening if `createCharacter()` is ever extended to validate against
> DQK's table too"*). `importDokParty.ts`'s `MAX_INFERRED_LEVEL = 8` search-range clamp was added M14
> (2026-07-03), two days before M93 gave DQK its own real level table, purely to keep every inferred
> level under CoK's flat cap since `createCharacter()` had no other table to validate against yet — a
> correct compromise at the time, never revisited once DQK's own uncapped-for-human table existed.
> Concretely reachable, verified against the real bundled `Death Knights of Krynn/SAVE/CHRDATA{n}.GAM`
> files (not hypothetical) via the real "⇪ Import DoK party → DQK" sidebar command: TANAR's real THAC0
> byte is an *exact* match (diff 0) for a level-10 Cleric, but the shipped importer reports her as
> level 7 (diff 2, HP 49 instead of 70) purely because the search never looked past 8. FLAVIUS
> (L7→L10, HP 42→60) and CELESTE (L6→L11, HP 30→55) are also affected; DRYDEN/LILLITH/NEACAIL
> (fighter/fighter/cleric-but-already-best-fit) are unaffected, confirmed as a negative control.
> Independently re-derived the exact same diffs/levels via a from-scratch vitest scratch reading the
> real save bytes through the real `thac0()`/`decodeDokSavedCharacter` production functions before
> trusting the audit's numbers. Fixed additively: added `CharacterRequest.levelCapRuleset?: 'cok'|'dqk'`
> (`character.ts`, default `'cok'` preserves every existing CoK/DoK caller unchanged); wired it into
> `createCharacter()`'s cap check (`dqkMaxLevel()` vs `maxLevel()`); `importDokParty.ts` opts in and
> widens `MAX_INFERRED_LEVEL` to 12 (the THAC0 table's own real ceiling, `combatTables.ts`'s `MAX_COL`);
> `dqkParty.ts`'s hand-authored heroes opt in too (preemptive — all 6 sit under both caps today, so no
> observed effect yet, but closes the identical latent silent-drop risk at near-zero cost). Both halves
> (wider search + `dqk` cap mode) had to ship together — verified that widening the search alone, before
> wiring the cap mode, would have flipped these three heroes from "silently underleveled" to "silently
> rejected outright" instead. Updated the existing e2e fixture's `hpFixedOk` literals, which had baked in
> the wrong (clamped) HP values as a passing assertion — the same "test certifies the wrong behaviour"
> shape M86/M89/M90 already established. New taxonomy sub-case: a caller can pre-emptively narrow its own
> search space specifically to avoid a validation gate's rejection path, hiding the same rule-mismatch
> M92/M93 named, one layer further upstream — nothing ever fails or errors, the import "succeeds," the
> numbers are just silently wrong. Full audit in `docs/engine/research/m95-audit.md`.

> Queue converged an 87th time — found while investigating the carried-forward "createCharacter() has

> Independently re-verified via a direct page-image render of `Champions of Krynn/Journal.pdf` (printed

> DEX 9, CON 10** — a materially easier DEX/CON bar than the buggy, Rose-borrowed one. Concretely
> reachable via the ordinary "Create New Character" screen (including its "Roll 4d6" convenience

> the Crown" instead of "Knight of the Sword," on both screens that display it. The existing unit test's

> "test bakes in a wrong value" pattern (M86/M89/M90/M95): here the assertion was correct, but its input
> never touched the boundary that would reveal the defect. Fixed: corrected the two values in

> (`window.__create.validate()`, no roster mutation needed). New taxonomy point: five rounds' worth of
> "is it wired?" checks gave zero signal about "is the wired data correct?" — the two require
> independent verification passes, and a confident doc comment ("verbatim") is not itself evidence of
> correctness. Full audit in `docs/engine/research/m96-audit.md`.

## Phase M97 — leaving DQK's own Town screen always routed back into Champions of Krynn's wilderness

> Not a data-fidelity bug like M92-M96 — a navigation bug. Since C4.3 (2026-06-22), DQK's own dungeon
> exploration ships a real, ordinary `(T)own` command (key `t`) that opens the shared `town.ts` Town
> hub screen — but `leaveTown()` (the only handler for selecting "Leave" or pressing Escape at the hub)
> unconditionally hardcoded `?wild=1` + `startWilderness()`, Champions of Krynn's own overland screen,
> because it was written hours before DQK's Town entry point existed and never learned it had gained a
> second caller. A DQK player pressing `t` then leaving Town was silently teleported into CoK's "Vale
> of Solace" with the DQK Heroes of the Lance roster now wandering a CoK map against CoK's own
> encounter tables — no crash, no console error, just the wrong game. Verified dynamically via a
> throwaway Puppeteer script driving a real headless session through the exact command sequence
> (`?dqk=1` → `openTown()` → select "Leave" → `location.search` flips to `?wild=1`, `window.__wild`
> boots live). `startTown()` already had a precedent (`levelCapRuleset`, M92/M93) for "this screen
> serves two games differently," but the exact same question was never asked of its one exit path.
> Fixed by mirroring that precedent: `startTown()` grew an optional `onLeave?: () => void` (every one
> of its 4 pre-existing callers passes none, behaviour unchanged); `dqkExplore.ts`'s `openDqkTown()`
> now supplies one that returns to `?dqk=1` + `startDqkExplore(activeAssetSource ?? undefined)` — the
> `activeAssetSource` reuse (not in the audit's own sketch) matters because a Library-loaded folder or
> an imported `.gbmod` would otherwise be silently discarded on the round trip, re-loading the bundled
> repo copy instead. Added a dedicated `runDqkTownLeave` e2e test (real click path via `__town.select`/
> `.activate()`, asserting `location.search` and a live `window.__dqk.mapIndex()`, not just URL/seam
> presence). New taxonomy: the M92/M93/M95 "gate built for game A, blindly reused by game B" shape
> applies to navigation/routing just as much as validation — and it's a harder-to-catch variant, since
> no `vitest` unit assertion on a pure function would ever surface a wrong *screen*, only a real
> DOM-driving e2e run does. Full audit in `docs/engine/research/m97-audit.md`.

## Phase C1 — the C64 corpus is a whole platform the loop cannot currently see

> **Why this section exists.** Seven complete C64 title sets (49 `.d64` sides, 4,426 PRG files, all
> reading clean) have been in the project since 2026-08-10 and two of their formats are already
> solved and committed — but `grep -i "c64|commodore|\.d64"` over this file returned **zero** hits,
> so the full-auto loop had no way to pick up any of it. That is the gap this section closes; the
> work items below are the honest current state, not a plan written ahead of evidence.
>
> Sources and their standing rules are in `CLAUDE.md` (read-only, never vendored;
> glob `<Title>\*.d64` **non-recursively** or the superseded damaged CoAB dumps get read back).
> Format writeup: `docs/engine/research/c64-disk-format.md`. Tools: `tools/c64_disk.py` (reader),
> `tools/c64_pic.py` (picture codec), `tools/c64_disasm.py` (6502).
>
> **The strategic point:** the C64 release is effectively an *unpacked* `.DAX` — assets are loose CBM
> files whose filename hex suffix is the DOS block id — so it is an independent oracle for DAX block
> identity, and its 6502 loaders are far easier to read than the x86 ones. Disassembling the C64
> consumer is what cracked the picture format below, the same technique that cracked the Amiga
> sub-frame codec. Careful: the 2-byte prefix is **rewritten** by the DOS port, so always compare
> payloads from offset 2.

  - [x] **C1.1** — pure-Python `.d64`/`.g64` reader (`tools/c64_disk.py`), verified against VICE's
    `c1541`; 49 sides / 4,426 files extract clean. **[2026-08-10]**
  - [x] **C1.2** — the fixed-size full-screen picture format SOLVED by disassembling `GDRIVE02`, the
    C64 blit overlay (`tools/c64_pic.py`, 15 tests, sha256 goldens for CoK/DoK/Gateway). Layout:
    two stacked 570-byte planes (screen map 38x15 + colour map) + 192 glyph bitmaps + 3 VIC
    background registers; glyphs `$00`-`$3F` come from a separate 514-byte `CHARSET`.
    `docs/engine/research/c64-disk-format.md` §7.4/§7.5. **[2026-08-11]**
  - [x] **C1.3** — Buck Rogers `PIC71`/`PIC72` SOLVED. Cracked by disassembling the `$C066`
    branch to completion rather than trying more offsets: control falls through the id compare
    and pointer decrement into the same generic glyph copy every other picture uses, so the
    destination is the only difference. All 37 fixed-size pictures now decode. Note the doc's
    "confirmed by rendering" framing was removed — the *uncorrected* decode of these two also
    renders plausible macro imagery, so visual coherence did not discriminate the hypotheses.
    **[2026-08-11]**
  - [x] **C1.4a** — TS VIC-II decoder landed (`packages/engine/src/loaders/c64Picture.ts`),
    reproducing the Python renderer's exact sha256 goldens for three real pictures on the same
    retail disks. Two independent implementations agreeing bit-for-bit. **[2026-08-11]**
